inherited.problem: 中文句子“后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼去探访时，她的实验室仍设备不足”里，离“她”最近的人是梅洛尼，读者会把实验室理解为梅洛尼的。英文明确写的是 Marie Curie's laboratory，中英两版因此不一致。
inherited.suggestion: 把“她的实验室”改为“居里夫人的实验室”。

inherited.problem: 中文把「took no copyright」接在“拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益”后面，并说“英译此处作”，读起来像是英译用这句话来表达“拒绝获利”。原文中 We took no copyright 是另起的一句，指没有申请版权保护。中文正文也没有说出这层意思。第二处「took out no patent」的“此处”同样指代不清。
inherited.suggestion: 改为“……皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益；他们没有申请版权（英译作「took no copyright」），把研究结果……”。第二处改为“没有申请专利（英译作「took out no patent」），也不在工业开发中保留任何好处”。

issues.problem: 英文 finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands 暗示她亲手接过了镭。证据说镭本身没有带到仪式上，她拿到的只是象征性的金钥匙。这与正文 hook 所强调的事实矛盾。中文“得到一克镭”没有这个问题。

issues.proposed: 改为 and a subscription raised by American women finally secured her a gram of radium。
issues.rationale: dek英文 finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands 改为 finally secured her a gram of radium，不再暗示她在仪式上亲手接过镭，与 hook 所述只交付金钥匙一致；中文“得到一克镭”本无此问题。

issues.problem: 开头（dek、hook.1）一再说“本书”“本书的引言”，但读者此时不知道是哪本书，要到 limits 才交代。梅洛尼第一次出现时，身份也只是“为本书写引言的人”，读者说不清她与此事的关系。

issues.proposed: 第一次提到时点明书名：“居里夫人1923年出版的《皮埃尔·居里》一书（梅洛尼为其写了引言）”。梅洛尼的身份写成“发起这次募捐、后来为该书写引言的梅洛尼”。不补加证据以外的身份信息。

issues.problem: “局”/the Bureau 没有说明是哪个机构，读者会困惑。证据本身也只写作 the Bureau。

edits.before: 一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和丈夫皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼在美国发起募捐，希望借此让她把研究继续下去。这笔账书里两边都有记载：梅洛尼在引言里记下了市价和募捐，居里夫人自己在自传笔记里算过放弃的那笔财富。

edits.before: A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and her husband Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use, and Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, set out to raise a subscription in America to enable her to go on with her work. The book records both sides of that account: Meloney's introduction notes the price and the subscription, and in her autobiographical notes Marie Curie reckons up the fortune she gave up.

edits.before: At one point (the book gives no year), Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history curriculum compulsory for medical students. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie Curie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: Pierre was doing double teaching, and the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

edits.before: 还有一件事，她在书里两处都写到。按她的叙述，在她同意之下，皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益，英译此处作「took no copyright」。他们把研究结果和制备镭的确切方法毫无保留地发表，来问的人也都得到答复。自传笔记里她又说了一遍：夫妇二人一贯不从发现中获取物质利益，方法从一开始就全部公开，没有申请专利，也不在工业开发中保留任何好处，此处英译作「took out no patent」。书里没写这个决定的日期。

edits.before: There is something else she writes about in two places in the book. In Marie Curie's telling, and with her agreement, Pierre Curie refused to draw any material profit from the discovery. As the English translation of the biography puts it, "We took no copyright": they published without reserve all the results of their research as well as the exact processes of the preparation of radium, and gave whatever information was asked of them. In the autobiographical notes she says it again: the two of them always refused to draw any material profit from the discovery, the process was published from the beginning, and they took out no patent and reserved no advantage in any industrial exploitation. The book gives no date for the decision.
edits.after: There is something else she writes about in two places in the book. In Marie Curie's telling, and with her agreement, Pierre Curie refused to draw any material profit from the discovery. They also took no copyright (the English translation of the biography reads "We took no copyright"), published without reserve all the results of their research as well as the exact processes of the preparation of radium, and gave whatever information was asked of them. In the autobiographical notes she says it again: the two of them always refused to draw any material profit from the discovery, the process was published from the beginning, they took out no patent (the translation reads "We took out no patent"), and they reserved no advantage in any industrial exploitation. The book gives no date for the decision.

edits.before: The money was still short. Inspired by their attempt, a French industrialist, Armet de Lisle, took what seemed at that epoch the daring step of founding a veritable radium factory to furnish the product to physicians, whose interest in the biological effects of radium and its possible therapeutic applications had been aroused by the publication of various investigations. The project proved a success because he could employ men already trained by the Curies in the delicate processes of the manufacture. Radium was now regularly placed on sale, at a high price it is true, given the special conditions under which it had to be made and the immediate rise in the cost of the minerals necessary to its production. Armet de Lisle, in an entirely disinterested manner, placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. Other funds were added either by the Curies themselves or through subventions, the most important of which, accorded by the Academy of Sciences in 1902, amounted to 20,000 francs.

The book goes on to say that, in an entirely disinterested manner, the industrialist placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. edits.before: Years later, in the autobiographical notes, she laid out the rest of the ledger. Radium is found in minerals in very small quantities, so its price is very high, and the profits of its manufacture have been great, since the substance is used to cure a number of diseases. What they sacrificed in renouncing the exploitation of their discovery, then, was a fortune, one that could after them have gone to their children. And what was even more to be considered, she wrote, was the objection of many of their friends, who argued "not without reason" that if they had guaranteed their rights they could have had the financial means of founding a satisfactory Institute of Radium, without the difficulties that had been such a handicap to both of them and were still a handicap to her. issues.problem: 开头出现的“局”（the Bureau）没有交代是什么机构。读者不知道它与赠镭的关系，只能猜。证据本身也没有给出全称。

evidence.quote: The tubes of radium presented to me were at the Bureau, whose officials had kindly offered to make the measurements

issues.proposed: 不补造全称，改为说明其角色，如“装镭的管子还在负责测量的那个‘局’（书中只称the Bureau）里”。

issues.problem: “射气”（emanations）是专业术语，开头首次出现时没有解释。一般读者难以理解“镭只用于为医院提取射气”意味着什么。

evidence.quote: the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use in cancer treatment

issues.proposed: 按证据补全用途：“只用于为医院提取射气、供癌症治疗”。英文同步补上 "in cancer treatment"。

issues.problem: “这笔账该书里两边都有记载”语序生硬，读起来拗口。
issues.proposed: 改为“这笔账的两面，书里都有记载”。

issues.problem: “学校”（the School）首次出现时没有说明是哪所学校、与居里夫妇是什么关系，读者分不清它和后文的索邦。

evidence.quote: Already in 1898, one of the laboratory chiefs of the School, G. Bemont, had given us temporary aid.

issues.proposed: 按证据说明角色，如“皮埃尔曾任实验室主任的那所学校的实验室主任之一贝蒙”。英文同步。

verify.overall: 定稿逐字段核对后，事实、归属、引语和中英对应均有证据支持，没有需要修正的事实问题；只有几处术语、机构称呼的易读性小问题和一处文风小问题可酌情改进。

issues.problem: 中文“后来为本书写引言的梅洛尼去探访时，她的实验室仍设备不足”中，离“她”最近的人是梅洛尼，读者容易把实验室理解为梅洛尼的。英文明确写作 Marie Curie's laboratory，中英不一致，也影响读者理解。

evidence.quote: Madame Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment

issues.proposed: 把“她的实验室”改为“居里夫人的实验室”。

issues.problem: 英文 finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands 暗示她亲手接过了镭。证据说镭本身没有带到仪式上，她拿到的只是象征性的金钥匙。这与正文 hook 所强调的事实矛盾。中文“得到一克镭”没有这个问题。

evidence.quote: The radium itself was not brought to the ceremony.

issues.proposed: 改为 and a subscription raised by American women finally secured her a gram of radium。

issues.problem: 开头（dek、hook.1）一再说“本书”“本书的引言”，但读者此时不知道是哪本书，要到 limits 才交代。梅洛尼第一次出现时，身份也只是“为本书写引言的人”，读者说不清她与此事的关系。

evidence.quote: to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each for the purchase of a gramme of radium

issues.proposed: 第一次提到时点明书名：“居里夫人1923年出版的《皮埃尔·居里》一书（梅洛尼为其写了引言）”。梅洛尼的身份写成“发起这次募捐、后来为该书写引言的梅洛尼”。不补加证据以外的身份信息。

issues.problem: “局”/the Bureau 没有说明是哪个机构，读者会困惑。证据本身也只写作 the Bureau。

evidence.quote: The tubes of radium presented to me were at the Bureau

issues.proposed: 写作“还在书中只称为‘局’（the Bureau）的机构里”，不补出机构全名。

issues.problem: 中文“为医科学生而设”与证据不符：证据说的是这门课对医科学生是必修。中文还漏掉了P.C.N.即物理、化学和博物课程这层说明，与英文不对等。

evidence.quote: the physics, chemistry and natural history course at the Sorbonne, obligatory for students of medicine

issues.proposed: 改为“索邦P.C.N.（医科学生必修的物理、化学和博物课程）的物理教席正好空缺”。

issues.problem: 中文把「took no copyright」接在“拒绝获取物质利益”之后，并说“英译此处作”，读起来像是英译用这句话表达“拒绝获利”。原文中这是另起的一句，意思是没有申请版权保护，中文正文没有说出这层意思。第二处「took out no patent」前的“此处”同样指代不清。

evidence.quote: With my agreement he refused to draw any material profit from our discovery. We took no copyright
We took out no patent and we did not reserve any advantage in any industrial exploitation.

issues.proposed: 改为“……皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益；他们没有申请版权（英译作「took no copyright」），把研究结果……”。第二处改为“没有申请专利（英译作「took out no patent」），也不在工业开发中保留任何好处”。

issues.problem: 证据 E9 只用“he”“his factory”指称，摘录中没有点名阿尔梅·德·利尔。正文直接写成德·利尔，并把 disinterested 译作“出于好意”，后者带有动机色彩。

evidence.quote: In an entirely disinterested manner he placed at our disposition a little working place in his factory

issues.proposed: 写作“书中接着写道，这位实业家不图回报地在他的工厂里给他们一小块工作地方……”。“出于好意”改为“不图回报”。

issues.problem: 英文直接用引号引出 "Yet, I still believe that we have done right."，没有标明这是本书英译本的措辞。story.2 标明了，这里没有，读者会以为是她的原话。

evidence.quote: Yet, I still believe that we have done right.

issues.proposed: 改为 ...all the same; in the English translation: "Yet, I still believe that we have done right."。

issues.problem: 中文“1902年科学院给的20,000法郎”中的“科学院”，容易与 context.0 的“维也纳科学院”混同。证据只写 the Academy of Sciences。

evidence.quote: one of the laboratory chiefs of the School, G. Bemont
